summary: Overview of building the AAPS app in a web browser with GitHub Actions instead of on a computer with Android Studio. The reader picks a method: AAPS Builder from an Android phone, or a GitHub fork plus a keystore preparation file from a computer or iPhone/iPad, then follows the four linked step pages. No app screens are involved; the labels are GitHub's and Google's.

sections.heading: Browser build
sections.summary: Page title and intro: the app can be built in the browser with GitHub Actions, from AAPS version 3.3.2.1 on.

sections.heading: Build yourself instead of download
sections.summary: Legal note: the APK cannot be downloaded and must not be shared; each user builds it for their own use.

sections.heading: Choose how to build
sections.summary: Introduces the two build methods, chosen by the device the reader builds from.

sections.heading: On an Android phone: AAPS Builder (recommended)
sections.summary: The recommended method: a setup page creates a private GitHub build repository; the reader downloads the built app from GitHub.

sections.heading: On a computer or an iPhone / iPad: fork and preparation file
sections.summary: The alternative method: fork the AAPS source on GitHub, make a keystore with a preparation file, and save the built app to Google Drive, switching between several browser tabs.

sections.heading: What you'll need
sections.summary: Accounts and tools needed for the fork method: Google account, GitHub account, a browser, and a helper (Simple Web Server or the iOS Files app) to run the preparation file.

sections.heading: The steps
sections.summary: The four steps of the fork method in order (fork, keystore, Google Drive authorization, build), with links to troubleshooting and optional operations.
